Subject: Capacity commitment options and phased GPU ramp — Acme Pharm

Hi Elaine & Jamal,

Thanks again for the time this week — great visibility into the batch/nearline and real-time inference mix for your MedImages product. Per our discussion, I put together three contract-friendly reservation options that balance unit cost and activation risk. Attached is a short deck and a sizing workbook that carries the assumptions we used.

Summary (high level):
- Option A — Minimal runway (cost-conscious): 8 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (min guarantee), 2-week warm-up window, burst to shared pool. Good for early production with lower steady-state throughput.
- Option B — Balanced (recommended): 24 GPUs min, 6-week phased ramp (8 -> 16 -> 24), can reserve warm standby for predictable latency at 99th percentile. Includes 10% monthly burst credits.
- Option C — Production scale (throughput-first): 64 GPUs min, immediate activation window with staged warm starts, guaranteed throughput lanes for model A and model B. Lower per-token cost; higher commit.

Key operational notes:
- We recommend KV-prefix caching for the MedImages pipelines to reduce token cost by ~18% once warmed.
- Quantization profile: int8 for batch jobs, fp16 for low-latency model variants.
- Canary plan: start with Option B canary at 8 GPUs for 30 days before moving to full 24 GPU floor.

Attachments: ACME_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf, cluster-sizing-workbook.xlsx (workbook shows expected token/sec and cost math).

Next steps: let me know which option you'd like priced with a 12 vs 24 month commitment and I can circulate an updated SOW. If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute technical alignment with Karthik to walk the warm-start/caching behavior.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the level set and clear options. A couple quick clarifying questions before we pull procurement in:
1) For Option B, can you confirm the SLA for 99th percentile latency once warm-starts are enabled? Our compliance team is sensitive to tail latency for triage flows.
2) How fast can we burst above the committed floor and is there an elasticity buffer for sudden model retraining (weekly batch runs)?

Also please confirm whether the 10% monthly burst credits are applied before or after invoice-level rounding / minimums.

If this looks good pricing-wise we’ll need the SOW to show a canary milestone and acceptance criteria for the warm-up.

Kim —

Short internal note to propose technical defaults I think will land with Acme: 
- SLA: with warm-start KV caching and a dedicated latency lane (slice of the 24 GPU pool pinned to model A), we can hit 99th latency targets of ~220ms for the fast model family. The trade-off is you need reserved warm standby (~1-2GB KV per worker) and a ~2 week prewarm.
- Burst: we can burst up to +40% of committed floor using shared burst capacity and pre-arranged hot spare allocations; these count against monthly burst credits. Extreme batch retraining should go to scheduled slot (we recommend nightly windows) — large ephemeral batch runs should be scheduled against a reserved burst window to avoid impacting p99.
- Canary plan: enable prefix caching, run synthetic load at 70% of expected QPS for 14 days, then escalate activation to 50% traffic for 7 days.

I attached a quick calculator in the workbook (tab: "operational_assumptions"). Happy to hop on a short call with Elaine if they want a deeper walkthrough.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity commitment options and phased GPU ramp — Acme Pharm

Elaine —

Quick answers inline: 
1) SLA / p99: With the warm-start configuration we outlined, p99 for the low-latency model family is contractually targetable at 250ms (we will put a 250ms p99 SLA in the SOW with the usual force majeure and maintenance windows carved out). Operationally we expect to be ~220ms after the 6-week ramp and caching warm-up.
2) Burst mechanics: Monthly burst credits are applied pre-invoice rounding and reduce billable consumed-burst tokens. You get a monthly bucket (10% of committed capacity expressed as compute-seconds) that is consumed first. Any overage after the bucket is billed at on-demand rates.

I attached an updated version of the options with an explicit canary milestone and acceptance criteria. If you’re comfortable we can price Option B for 12 vs 24 months and I’ll get a redlineable SOW over to procurement.

Proposed next step: we can do a technical canary kickoff week of Aug 21 — Karthik and Grace to lead the runbook, 30-day canary with acceptance gates.

Best,
Kimberly
